extracted.intended_audience: general readers, comedy fans, researchers of TV/stand-up history
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the format and production details of HBO's thirty-minute stand-up specials in which a single comedian performs a routine (usually live from The Fillmore). Useful for understanding the production/format requirements of this particular TV stand-up showcase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format: single comedian thirty-minute routine
rubrics_metrics.description: HBO Comedy Half-Hour is a stand-up comedy television series of specials by various comedians ... with the format of a single comedian presenting a routine for thirty minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each episode is structured as a half-hour showcase featuring one performer. Examples of comedians who appeared include Louis C.K., Janeane Garofalo, Chris Rock, Dave Chappelle, Patton Oswalt, Norm Macdonald, Margaret Cho, David Cross, and others (episode listings enumerate specific performers and dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Production/location: usually live from The Fillmore
rubrics_metrics.description: The series ... usually live from The Fillmore in San Francisco.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a live-audience, venue-based production style that likely influences staging, timing, and audience interaction in each half-hour set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running time: 30 minutes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episodes conform to a half-hour runtime, which constrains set length, pacing, and material selection for the performing comedian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre: stand-up comedy television specials
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre: Comedy; Original language: English; a stand-up comedy television series of specials by various comedians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions the show within televised stand-up — expectations include stand-up material (jokes, stories, observational or character-driven comedy) rather than sketch or variety formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network / original release context
rubrics_metrics.description: The series ran on HBO from 1994 to 1998 (Original release June 16, 1994 – January 16, 1998).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being an HBO program implies premium-cable standards (e.g., less restrictive language/content rules compared to broadcast TV) and a particular audience/branding context that can affect material choices and presentation.
